newsitem.title: UK: LME ends mixed, movements wide and baffling.
newsitem.headline: LME ends mixed, movements wide and baffling.

text.p: Base metal markets concluded a volatile and unpredictable Wednesday LME session mixed, with traders at a loss to gauge the complex's mood.
Copper and aluminium ended with pared losses, with the former metal recovering well from an early-afternoon decline that threatened to extend significantly lower.
However, the backwardation narrowed markedly, which suggested that the downside of the current $2,330/2,370 range should be favoured, traders said.
"I haven't got a clue at the moment. Its been one of those days when it has been all over the place," one said.
Prices briefly fell under $2,330, but did not uncover major stops that could have sent the market skidding under $2,330.
But after touching $2,322 prices bounced on covering to close the kerb at $2,338, still down $7 a tonne from Tuesday. The cash/threes backwardation was $46/47 against levels of $70 the previous day.

Aluminium made another foray towards the $1,700 target before the rise was squashed by tumbling copper prices. However, the solid physical undertone emanating from the U.S. restricted declines, and prices ended at $1,666, down $9.
Lead and zinc movements were wide throughout the session, with speculative interest driving prices higher before copper's downturn partially dampened sentiment.

Nevertheless both markets were resilient on the dips and pushed higher on the kerb. Zinc, which hit a fresh 4-1/2 year peak of $1,279 at one stage, closed at $1,275, a gain of $24, while lead ended at $693, up $22 from the previous kerb.
Traders said there was little fundamental impetus behind the strength of these markets, although expectations of high Japanese GSP zinc imports on April 1 were supportive for that metal.
Nickel trading was also variable, with prices fluctuating in line with copper's mood swings, before they trended upwards during the kerb.
Traders said the market was supported on dips towards the $8,000 level, and by the end of the kerb three months was $40 higher at $8,070.
Tin maintained the advances that started yesterday, aided by the contraction in the cash/threes contango and May tightness.

Cash/threes was near level at one stage, against $40 at the start of the week, before finishing around $7/10 contango. The backwardations in May reflect speculative rolling forward of positions, traders said.
Three months prices held the $6,000 level, and closed the session at $6,030, up $60.
The alloy market was quiet, and closed at a little-changed $1,545/50 a tonne.
